label: digit 1 input at original position 3
explanation: Fires when the token 1 is input at step 3 (the fourth original token). On dev it fires on every such step (precision 1.0), and those steps carry 98% of the activation mass. It also fires weakly (about 0.05-0.2 of max) when 1 is input at the neighboring positions t=2 or t=4. It never fires on any other token, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase, including when 1 is fed back as a copied input. Magnitude barely varies with L or the surrounding tokens; the top examples (about 0.95-1.0 of max) are all 1 at t=3.

issues: Weak firings off the predicate are real but small. On test, 1 input at t=2 fires 9% of the time (holding 1.1% of activation mass) and 1 input at t=4 fires 7% of the time (0.8% of mass). Together the misses hold 1.9% of the mass at about 0.05-0.23 of max. They explain why recall is 0.868 while mass recall is 0.981. They are a sparse, low-magnitude part of the feature, not a missed class.
Widening the predicate to (t in 2..4) & in_tok==1 gives test recall 1.0 but precision 0.40 and F1 0.57, which is worse than the original, so the original predicate stays.

All other claims check out on dev and test. The predicate has 0 false positives on test (precision 1.0). The feature never fires in the delimiter or copy phase, never fires on any token except 1, and t=3 carries 98.2% of the mass. The 45 activations at L=3 all come from t=2, because at L=3 step 3 is the delimiter.
